concepts.title: Guru Authority and Divine Instruction — When Surrender Becomes Necessary
concepts.excerpt: There are teachings that cannot be given through books or lectures. They cannot be understood through reading alone.

concepts.title: Guru-Student Transmission: Consciousness Transfer Between Organized Minds
concepts.excerpt: In the Mahayana understanding (and particularly in tantric Buddhist traditions), the relationship between guru (teacher) and student is not primarily pedagogical.

concepts.title: Pujari as Intermediary Between Worlds: The Priest's Dual Task
concepts.excerpt: A pujari (priest performing ritual) is tasked with something that sounds simple but is actually among the most complex work a human can do.

concepts.excerpt: A pujari (priest) faces an impossible task: simultaneously maintaining the ritual form (following procedures, timing, proper offerings) while also invoking and maintaining genuine divine presence.

concepts.title: The Priest Problem: Mediation Versus Direct Access in Spiritual Practice
concepts.excerpt: Imagine you want to contact the divine.

concepts.title: Ketchimyakyu: Blood Pulse Transmission
concepts.excerpt: Ketchimyakyu (血脈 — literally "blood pulse" or "bloodline") initially referred to the transmission of wisdom from a master to disciple—the passing of understanding through direct contact and relationship.

concepts.title: Living Transmission vs. Academic Study: Why Embodied Teaching Transforms
concepts.excerpt: A Sanskrit scholar can have read every major Tantric text. They can understand the philosophy intellectually.

concepts.title: Wandering Acarya: Transmission Through Continuous Movement and Direct Encounter
concepts.excerpt: In certain Buddhist traditions, particularly Zen and Forest Buddhism, the Wandering Acarya (teacher) is one who does not remain in a fixed monastery or teaching hall but continuously travels, encountering students in their own contexts and transmitting directly through the relationship that emerges in that encounter.

concepts.title: Transference Liberation: The Fire Metaphor
concepts.excerpt: In the Lakulisha Shaiva school and other forms of qualified non-dualism, liberation is understood not as merger with the Divine but as permanent proximity to it.

concepts.title: The Role of the Witness: Someone With Eyes to See
concepts.excerpt: Ramakrishna could break all the ritual rules. But there was no guarantee anyone would recognize what was actually happening.

concepts.title: Soul-to-Soul vs. Role-to-Role: Meeting at the Level of Consciousness
concepts.excerpt: Most human interactions happen at the level of roles. You're the customer, I'm the barista.

concepts.title: Warrior King vs Wisdom King: Two Models (Samuel)
concepts.excerpt: Two figures from early Indian narrative: Bharata of the Lunar Dynasty, in the Mahābhārata tradition, defined by his military conquests, his ritual sacrifices for victory, and his role as cakravartin — universal conqueror whose horse-sacrifice (aśvamedha) declares his territorial supremacy.

concepts.title: Janaka of Videha: The Wisdom-King Archetype
concepts.excerpt: In the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad, King Janaka of Videha holds a great sacrifice in his court and invites Brahmins from across the region.

concepts.title: Bhagavadgītā as a Sermon Calling the Alienated Young Back — Hein
concepts.excerpt: A young man from a good Brahmanical family has been wandering for six months with a band of forest renunciates.

concepts.title: Ramakrishna & Totapuri — The Integration of Opposite Paths

concepts.title: Guru-Dīkṣā Modernity Question: Is Transmission Requirement Traditional or Modern?

concepts.title: Ramakrishna Worshiping Holy Mother: The Final Teaching
concepts.excerpt: For decades, Ramakrishna practiced the three technologies of Tantra: Japa (mantra repetition), Puja (ritual worship), and Homa (fire offering).

concepts.title: Whicher: Yogasūtra as Responsible Engagement, Not World-Rejection
